questions.stem: What distinguishes Data Hierarchy from Data Taxonomy and Data Ontology?
options: Data Hierarchy is metadata while the other two present actual data
Data Hierarchy applies only to unstructured data
Data Hierarchy is used for security, the others for reporting
Data Hierarchy presents actual data, whereas Data Taxonomy and Data Ontology are metadata for Data Governance
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.explanation: Data Taxonomy and Data Ontology are metadata for the purpose of Data Governance, whereas Data Hierarchy presents actual data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is given as a well-known example of a Data Hierarchy?
options: An organisational chart running from the CEO down to the Database Administrator
questions.explanation: The organisational chart, starting from the CEO and going down to the Database Administrator, is the famous example; a family tree is another.

questions.stem: To what do Data Taxonomies apply?
questions.explanation: Data Taxonomies apply to identified objects or phenomena, whereas Data Ontologies apply to terms, concepts or categories.

questions.stem: To what do Data Ontologies apply?
questions.explanation: Data Ontologies apply to terms, concepts or categories.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the Data Hierarchy at database level?
options: Bits, Bytes, Database, Tables, Records, Columns
Database, Files or Tables, Records, Fields or Columns, Bytes, Bits
Records, Database, Tables, Bits, Bytes, Columns
Database, Bits, Bytes, Records, Tables, Columns
Tables, Database, Columns, Records, Bytes, Bits
questions.explanation: At database level the hierarchy runs Database, then Files or Tables, then Records, then Fields or Columns, then Bytes, then Bits.

questions.stem: What kind of parent-child relationship exists among the rows of a dataset in a Data Hierarchy?
options: Multiple parents and a single child
A single parent and multiple children
A single parent and a single child
questions.explanation: Like Data Taxonomy, Data Hierarchy has a single parent and multiple child relationship among the rows of the dataset.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT given as an example of a Data Hierarchy?
options: Database, Tables, Records, Columns, Bytes, Bits
A chain of relationships in actual data
questions.explanation: The examples are the organisational chart, the family tree and the database-level chain; a data dictionary is not one of them.

questions.stem: Why is data grouped into a Data Hierarchy?
options: So that data exploration and representation become easy
To eliminate the need for metadata
To prevent users from querying it
questions.explanation: Data can be grouped in a way where data exploration and representation become easy.

questions.stem: Which two terms are described as metadata used for the purpose of Data Governance?
questions.explanation: Data Taxonomy and Data Ontology are metadata for Data Governance; Data Hierarchy presents actual data.

options: A set of terms and concepts
A chain of relationship in actual data
questions.explanation: Data Hierarchy is a chain of relationship in actual data, such as the organisational chart or the family tree.
